newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat to hold "national unity" talks with Hamas.
newsitem.headline: Arafat to hold "national unity" talks with Hamas.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat will hold "national unity" talks on Wednesday with Moslem militant groups in defiance of Israeli demands for a crackdown on "terrorism".

Palestinian officials said on Tuesday the Gaza talks were a response to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's decision to seal off the West Bank and Gaza Strip after a double suicide bombing in Jerusalem killed 16 people on July 30.

"The talks are a national reaction...to the failed policy which is led by this stranger Netanyahu and reaction to the collective punishment...and siege (of Palestinian territories)," said Palestinian Supplies Minister Abdel-Aziz Shaheen after a preparatory meeting on Tuesday.

Shaheen brushed off Israeli charges that the talks, bringing together over a dozen groups including Arafat's ruling Fatah faction and the militant Hamas and Islamic Jihad movements, amount to Palestinian "appeasement of terrorism".

Netanyahu has accused Arafat of doing "damn all" to crack down on militants opposed to his interim peace deal with Israel and demanded action before Israel lifts sanctions imposed in the wake of the bombings.
"This is a refusal of the Israeli dictates to turn Yasser Arafat into a policeman getting orders from the Israeli Shin Bet (secret service)," Shaheen told Reuters.
"We refuse that and we challenge Netanyahu to come and uproot us."

Hamas boycotted the last Palestinian national meeting in April in protest at Arafat's continued detention of Hamas activists rounded up after a wave of bombings which killed scores of Israelis last year.
But leading Hamas figure Abdel-Aziz Rantissi said Palestinians had a united agenda for Wednesday's meeting, billed as the "National Unity Conference to Confront the Challenges".
"The top priority is to stand against the American and Israeli pressures which aim to strike against the Islamic movement's infrastructure," he said.
The Palestinian Authority and Hamas say at least 140 Islamist activists, mostly from Hamas, are still in Palestinian detention.
"We demanded the release of all the political detainees (held by) the Palestinian Authority," said Isa Nashar, who was a Hamas founder before he moved to the National Salvation Movement.
He said the Palestinian Authority had promised at Tuesday's meeting that Arafat would look into the issue.

The armed wing of Hamas claimed responsibility for last month's suicide attacks in a statement. Both Israeli and Palestinian officials have questioned its authenticity, but Netanyahu has said the indications point to Hamas involvement.
"The call to Hamas to participate in national talks does not bode well," Netanyahu's communications chief David Bar-Illan said last week.
"(Arafat) has been making agreements that flirt with terrorist organisations since the Palestinian Authority was established. We don't believe that this kind of appeasement works," he said.
The July 30 bombings and deepening crisis with Israel have overshadowed Arafat's previous troubles over investigations into corruption inside the Palestinian Authority.
A report last month recommended two ministers face trial and Arafat's cabinet offered collective resignation.
